subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron and heartbeat authority be solved as narrow per-job/heartbeat metadata now, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design in #71712?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent trust boundary determines who can create authority, where it is stored, how it is audited, and how existing wildcard cron/heartbeat setups upgrade.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one authority model.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-specific elevated approval metadata now, with execution-time checks and docs, while leaving broader scheduling provenance to a later RFC.

options.title: Reject Per-Job Elevation
options.body: Document the current allowlist-only model and require operators to manage privileged scheduled work outside OpenClaw or through strict existing allowlists.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one authority model.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the adjacent Gateway/agent cron caller-scope implementation and are the clearest routing owner for the cron side of the decision.
